turns.t: Um, hi doctor. I've been checking my blood pressure at home, because my mum said I should, and it's been high. Is that something?
It certainly could be. What have you been seeing? ~
Consistently high, in the morning and evening, for two weeks. Higher than the machine says is normal, anyway.
And how are you feeling?
Well, sometimes a bit of a headache. Otherwise fine.
Do you have any family history of blood pressure or heart problems?
Mum has high blood pressure. And my granddad had a heart attack.
Any allergies I should know about before we go on?
Latex. I get a rash when I wear the gloves at work, on my hands.
Noted. Any operations?
I had my appendix out, when I was fifteen.
Do you drink alcohol, or have a lot of caffeine or salt in your diet?
A few drinks at weekends, I suppose. I like crisps, though.
Any other medical conditions?
No, only the occasional migraine.
Is the home machine one that goes on your upper arm, and is it validated? ~
Upper arm, yes. I bought it from a pharmacy. It was recommended. ~
Good. I'd like to check it, can you bring it along sometime? ~
I can bring it Monday. ~
Right. High readings at home are often higher than in the clinic or lower, depending, so I won't diagnose from them alone. ~
That makes sense. I'm a bit worried though. ~
It's good that you checked. I'd say this is probably high blood pressure, but I want it confirmed properly.
How? ~
I'd like to arrange a 24-hour blood pressure monitor, which you wear on your arm for a day, and it takes readings every half hour.
Like a cuff that squeezes by itself? ~
Exactly. It's the gold standard. ~
Okay. Do I need tablets? ~
Not until we have the results. Many people with mildly raised readings start with lifestyle changes, so cut down on salt, crisps, and alcohol, and be active.
I can do the crisps. ~
And if you ever get severe headache with blurred vision, chest pain, or breathlessness, come in straight away.
I will. Thank you. ~
